newsitem.title: USA: Federal safety regulators open airbag probes.
newsitem.headline: Federal safety regulators open airbag probes.

text.p: Federal safety regulators are investigating complaints that airbags exploded prematurely in a probe that covers about 370,000 Mazda 626 sedans and Chevrolet Camaro coupes.

The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said it has received nine complaints of non-collision airbag deployments from Mazda drivers. Seven people received injuries, including minor burns and facial cuts.
The agency has received six similar complaints about Camaros, including one report that a driver-side airbag deployed after the car hit a pothole. One person was injured.
The investigations were part of NHTSA's monthly defect report, released on the Good Friday holiday, March 28. The air bag probes cover 170,000 1991-92 Camaros, and 200,000 1995-96 626 cars.
Mazda is a unit of Mazda Motor Corp. Camaro's are made by General Motors Corp.

Airbags have been blamed for the deaths of 62 children and small adults. In response to complaints that airbags are too powerful, NHTSA has revised its safety tests to allow automakers to install airbags that deploy with less force later this year.

NHTSA also said it has opened an engineering analysis to further study a total of 79 reports from Chrysler Corp. and consumers that the buckles on integrated child seats in 1995-97 minivans are malfunctioning. About 150,000 Dodge, Plymouth and Chrysler brand minivans are affected.
In some cases, the buckle has failed to release the harness belt. In others, children have been "choked" by the seat's "T-bar" because the harness continues to retract, according to the agency.
"In both situations, owners have been forced to cut the harness webbing in order to remove the child," the NHTSA report said.

Chrysler has told NHTSA the seats stop working because owners allow crumbs of food and drink residue to clog up the latching mechanism. NHTSA said it needs to gather more information and evaluate Chrysler's decision to not conduct a safety recall.

-- opened an investigation into an estimated 600,000 1989-90 Camrys from Toyota Motor Corp. because of leaking fuel tanks, and an undisclosed number of 1994 Camrys because of steering wheel separation complaints that have caused three injuries;
-- opened a probe into about 240,000 1995 Chrysler Neons for alleged fires in the steering column area;
-- upgraded an investigation into an estimated 680,000 1989-91 Dodge Monaco/Eagle Premier cars and 1990-93 Jeep Cherokee and Grand Cherokee sport utility vehicles for brake rotor problems;
-- upgraded an investigation into fuel tank leaks on an estimated 732,282 1996 Chrysler, Dodge and Plymouth minivans.
